advances: This is geometry for a nonempty lattice-excluded depth region of a probability measure. The contacts are on the auxiliary outer polytope, and the cap estimate uses the factor d+1.

proof:
The region $D_\alpha$ is the intersection of all closed halfspaces $K$ of mass $>1-\alpha$. Indeed, if $y\notin K$, a closed halfspace through $y$ in $K^c$ has mass $<\alpha$. Conversely, a closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$ with mass $<\alpha$ has an open complement of mass $>1-\alpha$, exhausted by parallel closed halfspaces strictly inside it. One has mass $>1-\alpha$ and excludes $y$. Also $D_\alpha\subseteq C$ by separation of points outside $C$.

The open complements of these large-mass halfspaces cover compact $S$. Select finitely many $K_i=\{w:v_i\cdot w\le k_i\}$ whose complements cover $S$. Let $C_m$ be compact polytopes containing $C$ in their interiors and converging in Hausdorff distance to $C$. For example, take the convex hull of the vertices of grid cubes of side $1/m$ meeting $C$, then add $[-1/m,1/m]^{n+d}$. The hull lies in the Euclidean $\sqrt{n+d}/m$ neighborhood of $C$ by convexity, and the addition preserves convergence. Set $Q_m=C_m\cap\bigcap_i\{w:v_i\cdot w\le k_i+1/m\}$. Each $Q_m$ contains $D_\alpha$ and has interior, since each point of the nonempty $D_\alpha$ is strictly feasible in this enlarged description. If arbitrarily large $m$ gave a point of $Q_m$ on the mixed lattice, boundedness and closedness of the mixed lattice would give a subsequential limit in $C$ on that lattice satisfying every original $K_i$. This contradicts their exclusion of $S$. Choose a sufficiently large $m$ and write $Q=Q_m$ using the inequalities of $C_m$ and the enlarged $K_i$. The strict exteriors of the former have mass zero, and those of the latter are contained in complements of mass $<\alpha$.

Write $P$ for the projection of $Q$. It is a full-dimensional compact polytope disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n$. For fixed $z$, Farkas' feasibility alternative for the system in $x$ says $z\in P$ exactly when $(\sum_i\lambda_i a_i)\cdot z\le\sum_i\lambda_i c_i$ for all $\lambda\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i\beta_i=0$. This nonnegative kernel is generated by vectors of minimal nonempty support. On a minimal support the restricted kernel has dimension one, since an independent kernel vector would permit a perturbation to a nonzero nonnegative vector with smaller support. Hence its support has size at most $d+1$, and there is only one ray per such support. Any nonnegative kernel vector decomposes into these rays by subtracting the largest possible multiple of a minimal-support vector with support in its current support and iterating with fewer positive coordinates. Thus the projected description is finite. Discard inequalities with zero base normal, which are tautologies because $P$ is nonempty. At a point in the relative interior of a facet of $P$ one remaining inequality must be tight. Its hyperplane contains the whole facet by relative interior and validity, so a positive rescaling gives the corresponding multipliers in the statement. At any lift on the facet the sum of its nonnegative constituent slacks with these positive multipliers is zero. This proves each contact equality.

Apply the lattice Helly theorem documented in fact 6d6fcf377e68c79c, with the continuous dimension there set to zero and integer dimension set to $n$, to the actual closed facet halfspaces of $P$. Their intersection misses $\mathbb Z^n$, so at most $2^n$ suffice, including the case when their full number is already at most $2^n$. At each $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ one selected facet is strictly violated. At any lifted point violating facet $j$ the positive sum of the constituent margins $a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x-c_i$ is positive. At least one constituent strict exterior therefore contains the point. Subadditivity and the individual exterior mass bounds prove the stated strict inequality.

statement:
Let $n\ge1$, $d\ge0$, let $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ be a convex body, and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability supported on $S=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)$. Fix $0<\alpha<1$. Suppose the ambient depth region $D_\alpha=\{y:\mu(H)\ge\alpha\text{ for every closed halfspace }H\ni y\}$ is nonempty and disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$. There is a compact full-dimensional ambient polytope $Q\supseteq D_\alpha$ disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, described by inequalities $a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x\le c_i$ with $\mu\{a_i\cdot z+\beta_i\cdot x>c_i\}<\alpha$.

Each facet $\ell_j\cdot z\le\delta_j$ of the base projection of $Q$ has a nonempty index set $I_j$ with $|I_j|\le d+1$ and positive multipliers $\lambda_{ji}$ such that
$$
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}\beta_i=0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}a_i=\ell_j\ne0,\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_j}\lambda_{ji}c_i=\delta_j.
$$
Every lifted point of $Q$ above that facet is tight in all inequalities indexed by $I_j$. At most $2^n$ of the facet halfspaces already have intersection disjoint from $\mathbb Z^n$. Their strict exteriors cover $S$, each exterior for facet $j$ having mass less than $|I_j|\alpha\le(d+1)\alpha$.
title: Finite projected facet certificates for a lattice-free depth region
